Main.dc.html.title: Google Analytics → All pages: a short chart, then the table, as Google Analytics lays it out

real.text:
Your real figures

ronins.co.uk, United Kingdom, last 30 days to 12 Oct 2026, read from the app on 13 Oct.

• Views a day: your website's line is Overview's (1,035 views); each page's line is its own screen's, and each adds up to its views in the table
• Every visit, view, conversion and change in the table is real
• Visits and conversion rate for each page are already collected: today's screen just doesn't show them

worked.text:
Worked out for this drawing

• The 30 days before: from the change the app shows today
• Content hub's 185 from 78 in What Hakken sees: kinds from Sites → Your pages; a page without one, by its address
• No visits 103: Your pages lists 161 pages and 58 of them were viewed

The built screen counts each of these exactly.

filters.text:
The filters, for you to agree

• Gains: 3 views or more up on the 30 days before (a new page counts from 0)
• Dropped: 3 views or more down
• Static: less than 3 either way
• No visits: on your website, but nobody viewed it in the period

Why 3: a page going from 1 view to 2 is "up 100%" and means nothing. The rule is written on the table, so nothing is hidden.

changed.text:
This round (13 Oct, after "too deep")

• One short, wide chart at the top, as Google Analytics draws it: your website dashed, the ticked pages as lines
• A tick box on each row picks what the chart draws, five at most so the lines stay readable; the five viewed most open ticked
• Filters beside the search box
• Both bar charts removed at your comments (13 Oct): the page is now the chart, then the table
• Dwell time added (engaged time a visit); conversion headings shortened to "Conv." and "Conv. rate", the full words on hover
• Still off the table: People (in the download and on each page's own screen)
• Two change columns: Views change beside Views, Conv. change last. Both are counts against the 30 days before (▲ 59, ▼ 2); the views % is on hover
